# Global Luxury Goods — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R6)

8 entities × 8 dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker | Key Brands |
|---|--------|--------|------------|
| 1 | LVMH | MC.PA | Louis Vuitton, Dior, Tiffany |
| 2 | Kering | KER.PA | Gucci, YSL, Bottega |
| 3 | Hermès | RMS.PA | Hermès |
| 4 | Richemont | CFR.SW | Cartier, Van Cleef |
| 5 | Prada Group | 1913.HK | Prada, Miu Miu |
| 6 | Burberry | BRBY.L | Burberry |
| 7 | Moncler | MONC.MI | Moncler, Stone Island |
| 8 | Brunello Cucinelli | BC.MI | Brunello Cucinelli |

---

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. Like-for-Like Growth vs Network Expansion + Currency**
Organic growth bundles 3 effects. Decompose FY2024 into:
- **Like-for-like (same-store)** growth
- Network expansion contribution (new DTC stores × maturity ramp)
- Currency impact
For each group, rank by "organic quality" (like-for-like as % of total organic).

**Q2. China Revenue Geographic Arbitrage Math**
Chinese consumers spend luxury in multiple geographies (Mainland, HK/Macau, Japan, France, Korea). For each group: (a) Mainland China revenue, (b) estimated **Chinese-origin consumer spending globally** (all geographies combined), (c) share of global revenue from Chinese customers. This is materially different from "Mainland China revenue" and drives real brand exposure.

**Q3. Louis Vuitton Revenue Reverse-Engineer (LVMH specifically)**
LVMH doesn't break out Louis Vuitton maison-specific revenue within Fashion & Leather. Using: (a) segment total €40B, (b) sell-side estimates + UBS Evidence Lab + Bain industry reports, (c) store count + productivity, **reverse-engineer Louis Vuitton revenue and operating margin**. Uncertainty range.

For other groups (not LVMH): identify their closest "analogous undisclosed" (e.g., Cartier within Richemont Jewelry, Gucci already disclosed).

**Q4. Full-Price vs Markdown Revenue Mix**
Each luxury group's "quality of sale": full-price ticket vs markdown-driven (outlet, seasonal). For each: estimate full-price share. Use: (a) outlet store count, (b) direct-to-outlet allocation %, (c) management commentary on discount discipline. Identify the most/least "markdown-dependent".

**Q5. Creative Director Transition Impact Quantification**
Luxury is vulnerable to creative director exits. Recent:
- Gucci: Sabato De Sarno appointed Jan 2023, Gucci -21% 2024
- Chanel: Virginie Viard out Jun 2024, replaced by Matthieu Blazy (from Bottega!)
- Bottega (Kering): Matthieu Blazy departed Jun 2024
- Dior: Maria Grazia Chiuri still in role (stable)

Estimate revenue impact per creative transition (12m post-appointment). Which group has most creative-transition-exposure?

**Q6. Second-Hand Value Retention Index**
Construct a "brand equity score" using:
- Average Birkin resale price (Hermès benchmark)
- Average Louis Vuitton resale retention
- Gucci resale discount vs retail
- Burberry resale discount
Rank 8 groups by resale value retention. Tie to wholesale pricing power.

**Q7. VIC Spend Elasticity to Macroeconomic Conditions**
VIC customers are less elastic (ultra-wealthy insulated from macro). Estimate each group's "**VIC elasticity**" = (FY24 VIC revenue Δ) / (Chinese top-1% wealth Δ). Lower elasticity = more insulated. Which groups are most/least VIC-protected in China slowdown?

**Q8. Japan 2025 Normalization Scenario**
Assume JPY strengthens to 140 (from 160 in 2024). Chinese inbound tourism to Japan +15% (vs 2024 +50%). For each group:
- Japan 2024 revenue baseline
- 2025E revenue assuming tourist spend -40% (yen normalization)
- Compensating domestic growth (+5%?)
- Net 2025 Japan revenue change
Identify which groups lose most Japan revenue in normalization.

# Global Luxury Goods — Deep Research Analysis

**Scope note:** FY2024 means calendar FY2024 for LVMH, Kering, Hermès, Prada, Moncler, Brunello Cucinelli; Richemont uses FY ended 31 Mar 2025; Burberry uses FY ended 29 Mar 2025. All figures are reported-currency unless noted. Estimates are marked where companies do not disclose the line item.

Core source base: LVMH FY2024 results and annual report ([LVMH results](https://www.lvmh.com/en/publications/lvmh-achieves-a-solid-performance-despite-an-unfavorable-global-economic-environment), [annual report](https://hosting.fluidbook.com/LVMH/2024interactiveannualreport/en/19-2024-Interactive-Annual-Report-LVMH.html)); Kering FY2024 results and URD ([results](https://www.kering.com/en/news/2024-annual-results/), [URD PDF](https://www.kering.com/api/download-file/?path=Kering_2024_URD_EN_f8c45e2e74.pdf)); Hermès FY2024 results ([release](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/02/14/3026433/0/en/Herm%C3%A8s-International-2024-Full-Year-Results.html)); Richemont FY25 results and annual report ([release](https://www.richemont.com/news-media/press-releases-news/richemont-posts-robust-performance-for-the-year-ended-31-march-2025/), [annual report PDF](https://www.richemont.com/media/ue1bjrjv/richemont-fy25-annual-report-en.pdf)); Prada FY2024 release and HKEX filing ([press release PDF](https://www.pradagroup.com/content/dam/pradagroup/documents/investors/FY-2024/Prada_Group_FY24_PR.pdf), [HKEX announcement](https://www.pradagroup.com/content/dam/pradagroup/documents/Shareholderinformation/2025/e-Announcement_of_the_Consolidated_results_for_the_period_ended_December_31_2024.pdf)); Burberry annual report ([annual report page](https://www.burberryplc.com/investors/annual-report-24-25)); Moncler annual report ([revenue page](https://www.monclergroup.com/documents/annual-report-2024/364-Moncler-Annual-Report-2024.html), [CSSG/channel page](https://www.monclergroup.com/documents/annual-report-2024/65-Moncler-Annual-Report-2024.html)); Brunello Cucinelli filings page and FY2024 release coverage ([IR archive](https://investor.brunellocucinelli.com/en/services/archive/investor/financial-reports/2024), [FashionUnited](https://fashionunited.it/news/business/ricavi-a-12-2-per-cento-per-brunello-cucinelli-nel-fy-2024/2025011326250)); Bain China/global luxury reports ([China 2024](https://www.bain.com/insights/2024-china-luxury-goods-market/), [global luxury 2024](https://www.bain.com/insights/luxury-in-transition-securing-future-growth/)); Rebag and The RealReal resale data ([Rebag PR](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/rebag-releases-its-fifth-annual-clair-report-a-comprehensive-luxury-appraisal-index-for-resale-302329096.html), [The RealReal 2024](https://www.therealreal.com/resale-report-24)).

## Q1. Like-for-Like Growth vs Network Expansion + Currency

Companies rarely disclose true same-store sales except Burberry and Moncler. Decomposition below uses disclosed constant-currency growth, disclosed CSSG where available, store/space commentary, and channel mix.

| Rank | Entity | FY24 revenue | Reported growth | Organic / CER | Est. like-for-like | Est. network / space | FX impact | Organic quality |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Prada | €5.43bn | +15% | +17% | +15.5% | +1.5% | -2% | ~91% |
| 2 | Hermès | €15.17bn | +13.0% | +14.7% | +12.0% | +2.7% | -1.7%, €235m | ~82% |
| 3 | Brunello Cucinelli | €1.28bn | +12.2% | +12.4% | +9.5% | +2.9% | -0.2% | ~77% |
| 4 | Richemont | €21.4bn | +4% | +4% | +3.0% | +1.0% | ~0% | ~75% |
| 5 | Moncler | €3.11bn | +4.2% | ~+7% est. | +3.0% Moncler CSSG | +4.0% | ~-2.5% | ~40-45% |
| 6 | LVMH | €84.68bn | -2% | +1% | +0.3% | +0.7% | -2%, scope -1% | ~30% |
| 7 | Kering | €17.19bn | -12% | -12% | -13% DTC/traffic | +1% est. | ~0% | N.M., negative |
| 8 | Burberry | £2.46bn | -17% | -15% | -12% CSSG | +1% space; wholesale drag -4% | -2% | N.M., negative |

**Read-through:** Prada and Hermès had the highest-quality growth: Prada explicitly says retail growth was driven by like-for-like, full-price volumes; Hermès had broad regional growth with controlled store expansion. Moncler’s headline growth relied more on space/channel ramp than same-store. Kering and Burberry were not “low quality growth”; they were negative same-store cases.

## Q2. China Revenue Geographic Arbitrage Math

Bain estimates Mainland China luxury spending fell 18-20% in 2024, with overseas shopping, especially Japan, the main offset. Companies disclose geography by destination, not customer nationality, so Chinese-origin exposure is estimated.

| Entity | Mainland China revenue, est. | Chinese-origin global spend, est. | Chinese-origin share of group revenue | Main inference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| LVMH | €10-12bn | €23-25bn | 27-29% | Asia ex-Japan €23.25bn plus large Chinese spend in Japan/Europe. |
| Kering | €2.7-3.2bn | €5.0-5.5bn | 29-32% | Gucci APAC fell sharply; Chinese tourism shifted to Japan. |
| Hermès | €3.4-3.8bn | €4.0-4.5bn | 26-30% | Greater China traffic weak, but Japan/local VIC mix resilient. |
| Richemont | €3.3-3.8bn | €5.7-6.3bn | 27-30% | APAC 33% of sales; China/HK/Macau -23%, but jewelry VIC and tourism offset. |
| Prada | €0.9-1.0bn | €1.6-1.8bn | 30-33% | APAC retail €1.60bn, Japan €656m, strong Chinese tourist arbitrage. |
| Burberry | £0.6-0.7bn | £0.75-0.85bn | 30-34% | APAC £1.04bn; Mainland China -15%, Japan +1% boosted mainly by Chinese tourists. |
| Moncler | €0.65-0.75bn | €0.9-1.0bn | 28-32% | Mainland China grew double digit, but Japan/Korea also meaningful. |
| Brunello Cucinelli | €0.13-0.16bn | €0.22-0.26bn | 17-20% | Asia is ~28% of sales; China exposure is structurally lower than peers. |

**Key conclusion:** Mainland revenue materially understates true China risk for LVMH, Kering, Prada, Burberry, and Richemont because Chinese shoppers migrated spend to Japan and Europe. It overstates neither Hermès nor Brunello, where local/VIC and non-China mix are more important.

## Q3. Louis Vuitton Revenue Reverse-Engineer

LVMH discloses Fashion & Leather Goods revenue of €41.06bn and recurring operating profit of €15.23bn, a 37.1% segment margin. Louis Vuitton maison revenue is not disclosed.

| Step | Derivation |
|---|---:|
| LVMH Fashion & Leather Goods FY24 revenue | €41.06bn |
| Estimated non-LV maisons: Dior Couture, Celine, Fendi, Loewe, Loro Piana, Marc Jacobs, Givenchy, Rimowa, etc. | €19-22bn |
| Residual Louis Vuitton revenue | **€19.5-22.5bn** |
| Store/productivity cross-check | ~430-470 LV stores × €42-48m/store = ~€18-23bn |
| Segment operating profit | €15.23bn |
| Estimated LV operating margin | **42-47%** |
| Estimated LV operating profit | **€8.4-10.1bn** |

**Central estimate:** Louis Vuitton revenue ~€20.8bn, operating margin ~45%, operating profit ~€9.4bn. Exact UBS Evidence Lab or sell-side datasets are not public in the filings inspected, so the fallback is residual brand math plus store productivity.

Analogous undisclosed items:

| Group | Closest analogous undisclosed item | Estimate / note |
|---|---|---|
| Kering | Gucci is disclosed | Gucci revenue €7.65bn, margin 21.0%; no reverse engineering needed. |
| Hermès | Birkin/Kelly/Constance mix inside Leather Goods | Leather Goods €6.46bn; bag-line split not disclosed. |
| Richemont | Cartier within Jewellery Maisons | Jewellery Maisons €15.33bn; Cartier est. €9.5-10.5bn; Van Cleef est. €4-5bn. |
| Prada | Miu Miu FY revenue | Miu Miu growth disclosed at +93%; FY revenue not disclosed; est. €1.5-1.8bn retail scale. |
| Burberry | Outerwear/scarf franchise | Product categories disclosed, trench/scarf split not disclosed. |
| Moncler | Moncler brand disclosed, sub-lines not | Moncler €2.71bn; Stone Island €0.40bn. |
| Brunello | Product/VIC split | Retail/wholesale disclosed; product and VIC revenue not disclosed. |

## Q4. Full-Price vs Markdown Revenue Mix

| Rank | Entity | Est. full-price share | Markdown dependence | Evidence / logic |
|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Hermès | 98-99% | Minimal | Scarcity, allocation, controlled distribution. |
| 2 | Brunello Cucinelli | 95-97% | Very low | High-end wholesale/retail, limited promotional posture. |
| 3 | Richemont | 92-95% | Low | Jewelry maisons dominate; some watch wholesale discounting. |
| 4 | Prada | 92-95% | Low | FY24 retail growth explicitly driven by full-price volumes. |
| 5 | LVMH | 91-94% luxury maisons; lower including Sephora/DFS | Low-medium | LV/Dior high full-price; DFS/beauty retail dilutes group average. |
| 6 | Moncler | 87-90% | Medium | DTC strong, but seasonal apparel and factory outlet channel matter. |
| 7 | Kering | 83-87% | Medium-high | Gucci transition, inventory reduction, wholesale cleanup. |
| 8 | Burberry | 68-75% | Highest | 54 outlets out of 422 DOS; wholesale £319m; brand reset and weaker sell-through. |

Most markdown-dependent: Burberry, then Kering. Least markdown-dependent: Hermès, Brunello, Richemont jewelry.

## Q5. Creative Director Transition Impact Quantification

Correction to the prompt timing: Chanel’s Virginie Viard exit was June 2024, but Bottega’s formal transition was announced in December 2024; Kering says Louise Trotter joined Bottega at end-January 2025.

| Entity | Transition exposure | FY24 / 12m impact estimate |
|---|---|---:|
| Kering | Highest: Gucci, Bottega, Alexander McQueen | Gucci -21% comparable = ~€2.1bn revenue loss vs 2023; brand-specific creative/repositioning drag est. €1.2-1.5bn after macro adjustment. |
| Burberry | Daniel Lee repositioning still flowing through | FY25 CER revenue -15%; creative/assortment drag est. £150-250m after macro/channel adjustment. |
| LVMH | Dior stable; LV menswear shift lower risk; Celine/Givenchy transitions smaller | Group impact limited, est. <1% of revenue. |
| Prada | Miuccia Prada/Raf Simons and Miu Miu momentum stable | Positive creative contribution; Miu Miu +93% retail growth. |
| Moncler | Less single-designer dependent, Genius/collab model | Low; more product/weather/channel risk than CD risk. |
| Richemont | Jewelry maisons less fashion-CD sensitive | Low. |
| Hermès | Artisanal/house-code model | Very low. |
| Brunello Cucinelli | Founder-led continuity | Very low. |

Most exposed: Kering by a wide margin.

## Q6. Second-Hand Value Retention Index

Index is anchored to Rebag 2024 value retention: Hermès 100%, Louis Vuitton 88%, Chanel 92%, Goyard 104%. Rebag also reported Prada/Miu Miu improvement; The RealReal search data showed Louis Vuitton, Prada, Gucci, Miu Miu, Bottega, Dior among top searched brands.

| Rank | Entity | Resale retention index | Brand equity / pricing read-through |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | Hermès | 100 | Birkin/Kelly scarcity supports full-price power and no markdown culture. |
| 2 | LVMH | 82 | LV 88% is best-in-class outside Hermès/Goyard/Chanel; Dior/Tiffany supportive. |
| 3 | Richemont | 76 | Cartier and Van Cleef jewelry retain value well; watches more mixed. |
| 4 | Prada | 66 | Miu Miu/Prada improving; still below LV/Hermès retention. |
| 5 | Kering | 55 | Gucci resale discount remains material; Bottega/YSL partly offset. |
| 6 | Moncler | 50 | Outerwear resale decent but apparel is less liquid than handbags/jewelry. |
| 7 | Brunello Cucinelli | 46 | Quiet-luxury apparel retains less than iconic bags/jewelry despite strong primary pricing. |
| 8 | Burberry | 38 | Outlet presence and apparel mix weaken resale floor. |

Wholesale pricing power tracks the same ranking: Hermès/LV/Cartier can restrict supply; Burberry and Gucci need more channel discipline to rebuild resale floors.

## Q7. VIC Spend Elasticity to China Macro

No company discloses FY24 China VIC revenue change. I use a central assumption that Chinese top-1% wealth fell ~4% in 2024, reflecting property/market pressure, and estimate VIC revenue change from regional disclosures and Bain’s China luxury decline.

Formula: `VIC elasticity = estimated FY24 China VIC revenue change / (-4%)`.

| Entity | Est. FY24 China VIC revenue change | Signed elasticity | Protection read |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Hermès | +1% | -0.25x | Best true VIC insulation. |
| Richemont | -1% | +0.25x | Jewelry VIC resilient; watches weaker. |
| LVMH | -2% | +0.50x | LV/Dior VIC resilient, but broader Chinese base softer. |
| Brunello Cucinelli | +3% | -0.75x | Good insulation, but China base is smaller. |
| Moncler | +4-6% | -1.0x to -1.5x | Growth more brand/category driven than pure VIC. |
| Prada | +4-6% | -1.0x to -1.5x | Miu Miu cycle overwhelms macro; not purely VIC-protected. |
| Kering | -9% to -11% | +2.3x to +2.8x | Gucci exposed to aspirational China slowdown. |
| Burberry | -12% | +3.0x | Least protected; Mainland China -15%, Japan tourist support only partial. |

Most VIC-protected in a China slowdown: Hermès, Richemont jewelry, LVMH high-end maisons, Brunello. Least protected: Burberry and Kering.

## Q8. Japan 2025 Normalization Scenario

# Global Luxury Goods — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R6)

**Sources used (primary):** LVMH 2024 FY press release (lvmh.com 28-Jan-2025); Kering 2024 Annual Results (kering.com 10-Feb-2025); Richemont FY25 results (year ended 31-Mar-2025, richemont.com 16-May-2025); Hermès 2024 FY presentation (finance.hermes.com); Prada Group FY24 release (pradagroup.com 4-Mar-2025); Burberry FY25 prelim release (burberryplc.com 14-May-2025); Moncler FY24 deck (monclergroup.com 13-Feb-2025); Brunello Cucinelli FY24 release (investor.brunellocucinelli.com 13-Mar-2025). Sell-side triangulation: Bernstein/Solca, BoF "Luxury's First €20B Brand", UBS Evidence Lab.

---

## Q1. Organic Growth Decomposition — FY2024 (LFL vs Network vs FX)

Companies do not all decompose organic the same way; below are best-evidence triangulations from each release.

| Group | Reported Δ | FX | **Organic** | LFL est. | Network est. | **Organic Quality (LFL/Organic)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hermès | +13% | −2pp | **+15%** (cc) | +13% | +2% | **~87%** |
| Prada Group | +15% | −2pp | **+17%** (cc; LFL retail +18%) | +14% | +3% | **~82%** |
| Brunello Cucinelli | +12.2% | ~0 | **+12.4%** | +9% | +3% | **~73%** |
| Moncler Group | +6% | −1pp | **+7%** (cc) | +4% | +3% | **~57%** |
| LVMH | −2% | −2pp | **+1%** | ≈0 | +1% | **~50%** (very thin LFL) |
| Richemont (FYE Mar-25) | +4% | 0 | **+4%** (cc) | +1% | +3% | **~25%** |
| Kering | −12% | 0 | **−12%** | −13% | +1% | **LFL deeply negative** |
| Burberry (FY25, FYE Mar-25) | −17% | −2pp | **−15%** (cc; comp store −12%, space +1%) | −12% | +1% | **LFL deeply negative** |

**Ranking by organic quality:** Hermès > Prada > Cucinelli > Moncler > LVMH > Richemont > Kering ≈ Burberry. Hermès' +15% is almost entirely LFL (price + traffic on existing doors) — the highest-quality growth profile in the sector. Prada's "+18% retail driven by LFL full-price volumes" (per company language) is strikingly clean. Burberry and Kering have *negative* LFL — meaning network expansion is the only thing partially offsetting same-store erosion.

---

## Q2. China Revenue Geographic Arbitrage Math

Disclosure asymmetry: only Richemont/Hermès/LVMH publish broad regional breakdowns; "Asia ex-Japan" is the closest mainland China proxy. Chinese-origin global spend is multiplier 1.6–2.2× of Mainland disclosed (Bain China Luxury 2024 report; tourist redirection to Japan & Europe in 2024).

| Group | Mainland CN rev (est.) | Est. Global Chinese-origin Spend | % of Group Rev from Chinese customers |
|---|---|---|---|
| LVMH | ~€13B (≈30% of Asia ex-Japan €27B) | **~€23–26B** | **27–31%** |
| Kering | ~€2.7B (Gucci ~35% Asia-Pac of €7.7B) | **~€4.5–5.0B** | **27–30%** |
| Hermès | ~€3.5B (Asia ex-Japan €7.4B, ~half) | **~€5.5–6.0B** | **35–40%** (highest among large caps) |
| Richemont | ~€4.0B (Asia-Pac €5.6B contracted) | **~€6.5–7.5B** | **30–35%** |
| Prada Group | ~€1.3B (APAC €1.4B retail of €4.8B) | **~€2.0–2.3B** | **38–43%** (Miu Miu Chinese-skewed) |
| Burberry | ~£0.5B (~20%) | **~£0.9–1.1B** | **~35%** |
| Moncler | ~€0.85B (Asia €1.34B; ~64%) | **~€1.3–1.5B** | **42–48%** *(most exposed)* |
| Cucinelli | ~€140M (~11% Asia 27% × China share) | **~€220–280M** | **~17–21%** *(least exposed)* |

**Insights:** Moncler and Prada Group have the highest *real* Chinese-consumer share (Asia + Japan tourist + EU tourist combined). Cucinelli is the most insulated (US/EU HNW core). LVMH Mainland may be ~16% of group, but global Chinese exposure is ~30%.

---

## Q3. Louis Vuitton Reverse Engineering + Analogous Undisclosed

LVMH F&L FY24 = **€41.06B revenue** / **€15.23B EBIT** / **37.1% margin** (LVMH press release). LVMH does not break out LV.

**Triangulation methods for LV FY24:**
- **(a) Top-down residual:** Dior Couture est. €9.0–9.5B (peer-checked vs BoF, Bernstein); Fendi/Celine/Loewe/Loro Piana/Givenchy/Marc Jacobs/Pucci/Berluti/Rimowa combined ~€7.5–8.5B → LV residual = **€41.06B − €17B − €8B = ~€23–24B**.
- **(b) Productivity bottom-up (UBS Evidence Lab template):** ~470 LV directly operated stores × ~$45–48M average productivity (Bernstein/Solca) ≈ **$22–24B ≈ €20.5–22.5B** at 2024 avg EUR/USD 1.08.
- **(c) BoF 2023 milestone "first €20B brand" + reported FY23–24 LV "moderate decline" implied → 2024 LV ≈ €20–21B (lower bound) to €24B (upper bound).**

**Triangulated LV FY24 estimate: €21–24B revenue (mid €22.5B) ≈ 52–58% of F&L.**

**LV operating margin:** Triangulating LV-implied EBIT — at F&L EBIT €15.23B and LV ~65–70% of F&L profit pool (since Dior/Loro Piana lower margins than LV), LV EBIT ≈ €10–11B → **LV op margin ≈ 42–48%, midpoint ~45%**. Uncertainty range: ±300 bps.

**Analogous undisclosed within other groups:**

| Group | Largest undisclosed sub-maison | Est. revenue | Est. op margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Richemont | **Cartier** (within Jewellery €15.3B) | ~€10.5–11.5B | ~32–35% |
| Richemont | Van Cleef & Arpels | ~€3.0–3.5B | ~36–40% |
| LVMH | Dior Couture | ~€9.0–9.5B | ~30–35% |
| LVMH | Tiffany | ~€4.5–5.0B | low/mid-teens |
| Kering | Balenciaga | ~€1.5–1.7B (within Other Houses €3.2B) | ~5–8% |
| Kering | Boucheron + Pomellato + Qeelin | ~€0.8–1.0B combined | mid-teens |
| Hermès | "Leather Goods & Saddlery" division | €6.7B disclosed | ~50% inferred |
| Prada | Miu Miu | **disclosed** €1.23B (+93% LFL retail) | ~28–32% est. |
| Moncler | Stone Island | **disclosed** €397M (+0%); DTC €209M +23% | ~12–15% |

---

## Q4. Full-Price vs Markdown Mix

Triangulated using outlet count, mgmt commentary on direct-to-outlet allocation, and Bain "Quality of Sale" dimension.

| Group | Outlet/factory stores | Direct-to-outlet alloc. | Discount discipline | **Full-Price Share (est.)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hermès | **0** | 0% | Strict — products destroyed/recycled, never marked down | **~98%** |
| Cucinelli | minimal (Solomeo HQ outlet only) | <5% | Founder-led discipline; full-price dogma | **~93–95%** |
| LVMH (LV maison) | 0 | 0% | No discounting policy | **~97%** (LV) / **~85%** group blended |
| Moncler | ~25 outlets | ~8% | Price-disciplined; Stone Island slightly looser | **~88%** |
| Prada Group | ~50 outlets | ~10–12% | "Like-for-like full-price volumes" (mgmt language Q4-24) — improving | **~85%** |
| Richemont | watch outlets, jewelry full-price | ~10% | Hard-luxury structurally resilient | **~85%** |
| Kering (Gucci) | ~85–90 outlets | ~18–22% | Mgmt explicitly pulling wholesale; outlet exposure remains material | **~70%** |
| Burberry | ~50 outlets | **~25–30%** | Schulman explicitly cutting markdown reliance, but base is highest in peer set | **~62–65%** |

**Most markdown-dependent: Burberry**, then Kering/Gucci. **Least: Hermès** (structural zero-markdown), with Cucinelli and LV close behind.

---

## Q5. Creative Director Transition Impact (~12 months post)

Empirical template (Burberry 2018 Tisci, YSL 2012 Slimane, Celine 2018 Slimane, Bottega 2018 Lee): year-1 typically −5% to −10% LFL; year-2 flat; year-3 +5–15% if collections resonate. Magnitude scales with creative reset depth.

| Recent transition | Realized / est. 12m LFL impact |
|---|---|
| **Gucci / Sabato De Sarno** (appointed Jan-23, debut Sept-23) | **Realized: Gucci −21% comparable in FY24** (Kering release). Reset disrupted the Alessandro Michele archetype. De Sarno departed Feb-2025. |
| **Bottega Veneta / Matthieu Blazy → Louise Trotter** (Blazy departed Jun-24) | Bottega still **+6% comp FY24** under Blazy carryover collections; risk crystallizes in FY25–26. Est. **−5 to −10%** transition drag. |
| **Chanel / Virginie Viard → Matthieu Blazy** (Dec-24) | Private; analyst est. **0 to −5%** in 2025 (Chanel revenue ~$20B+) |
| **Celine / Hedi Slimane → Michael Rider** (Oct-24) | Est. **−10 to −15%** as Slimane base resets |
| **Givenchy / Sarah Burton hire** (LVMH press release confirms) | Est. flat to −5% |
| **Burberry / Daniel Lee + Schulman CEO reset** | **−15% realized FY25**; transition + macro |
| **Dior / Maria Grazia Chiuri** (status uncertain at FY24; Jonathan Anderson speculation) | Stable; risk building |

**Most creative-transition exposed: Kering** — Gucci, Bottega, Balenciaga, McQueen and YSL all in some state of creative reset; ~70%+ of group EBIT at risk. **Least exposed: Hermès** (Nadège Vanhée-Cybulski since 2014), **Cucinelli** (founder-designer), **Moncler** (Genius platform model is collection-distributed, not auteur-dependent).

---

## Q6. Second-Hand Value Retention Index

Composite from Vestiaire Collective, Sotheby's, Rebag Clair Report, StockX (where applicable).

| Group | Hero item retention | Group blended | **Score (0–100)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hermès | Birkin 30 Togo: ~120–140% of retail (often appreciates) | ~85% | **100** |
| Richemont (Cartier/VCA) | Love bracelet ~80–90%, Santos watch ~80%, Alhambra ~75% | ~78% | **88** |
| LVMH (LV) | Neverfull MM ~70–75%; vintage mono higher; Tiffany Lock ~60% | ~65% | **76** |
| Prada Group | Galleria ~50–55%, **Miu Miu Arcadie ~70–80%** (top mover 2024) | ~58% | **66** |
| Moncler | Maya/Maya 70 ~45–55% | ~45% | **52** |
| Cucinelli | Limited, illiquid resale (sweaters, RTW) — ~35–45% | ~40% | **45** |
| Kering (Gucci) | Marmont ~30–40%; Jackie reissues stronger ~50% | ~38% | **42** |
| Burberry | Trench ~30–35%; logo accessories ~20–25% | ~28% | **30** |

**Ranking: Hermès > Richemont > LVMH > Prada > Moncler > Cucinelli ≈ Kering > Burberry.** Resale retention correlates tightly with wholesale pricing power and ability to push annual price increases without LFL volume loss — exactly the Q1 ranking pattern.

---

## Q7. VIC Elasticity to Chinese Macro

Chinese top-1% wealth proxy 2024 ≈ −5% to −7% (Hurun; UBS Global Wealth). Define Elasticity ε = %Δ VIC revenue ÷ %Δ Chinese top-1% wealth. **Lower (or negative) = more insulated.**

| Group | FY24 China/VIC revenue dynamic | Implied ε | Insulation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hermès | Total +15% cc; China resilient; VIC channel grew | ≈ **−2.5** (grew despite downturn) | **Most insulated** |
| Cucinelli | China double-digit growth (mgmt commentary FY24) | ≈ **−1.8** | Very insulated |
| Richemont Jewellery (Cartier high jewellery) | +8% group; HJ globally strong; CN soft | ≈ **−0.4** | Insulated at the top end |
| Moncler | Asia +6%; high-end strong, mid-tier soft | ≈ **+0.3** | Mixed |
| Prada Group | APAC +13%; Miu Miu propelling | ≈ **−1.0** | Surprisingly insulated via Miu Miu | 
| LVMH (ex-aspirational) | F&L organic 0%; Asia ex-Japan negative; W&S cognac weak | ≈ **+0.5** | Moderate |
| Kering (Gucci) | Asia-Pac comp deeply negative; "VIC" base aspirational | ≈ **+3.5** | **Most exposed** — large aspirational base mistaken for VIC |
| Burberry | Asia comp double-digit decline | ≈ **+3.0** | Highly exposed — aspirational core |

**Most VIC-protected:** Hermès, Cucinelli, Richemont High Jewellery / Cartier. **Least:** Kering (Gucci) and Burberry — their "VIC" tier is largely middle-affluent aspirational shoppers, whose spend is highly macro-elastic.

---

## Q8. Japan 2025 Normalization Scenario

Assumptions: USD/JPY 160 → 140 (−12.5%); Chinese inbound +50% in 2024 → +15% in 2025; tourist spend on luxury **−40%** vs 2024; domestic +5%. Japan's tourist-share of in-country luxury sales averaged 50–60% in 2024 (Bain/Altagamma).

| Group | Japan 2024 rev (est.) | Tourist share | 2025E tourist rev | 2025E domestic rev | **Net Δ vs 2024** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LVMH | ~€7.0B (8–9% of group; mgmt: "double-digit Japan growth in 2024") | ~55% | −40% on €3.85B = €2.31B | +5% on €3.15B = €3.31B | **~€5.62B → −20%** |
| Hermès | ~€2.0B (Japan 9% of €15.2B; Statista) | ~50% | −40% on €1.0B = €0.60B | +5% on €1.0B = €1.05B | **~€1.65B → −18%** |
| Richemont (Japan +25% in FY25, ~12% mix) | ~€2.5B | ~55% | −40% on €1.38B = €0.83B | +5% on €1.13B = €1.18B | **~€2.01B → −20%** |
| Kering | ~€1.3B (Japan ~7–8%; Q4 trends worsened in Japan per release) | ~60% | −40% on €0.78B = €0.47B | +5% on €0.52B = €0.55B | **~€1.02B → −22%** |
| Prada Group | Japan +46% in 2024 (best region); ~14% mix → ~€0.75B | ~55% | −40% on €0.41B = €0.25B | +5% on €0.34B = €0.35B | **~€0.60B → −20%** |
| Moncler | Asia inc. Japan strong; Japan ~12–14% → ~€0.42B | ~45% | −40% on €0.19B = €0.11B | +5% on €0.23B = €0.24B | **~€0.36B → −15%** |
| Burberry | Japan ~9% → ~£220M | ~40% | −40% on £88M = £53M | +5% on £132M = £139M | **£192M → −13%** |
| Cucinelli | Japan ~7–8% → ~€90M | ~35% | −40% on €31M = €19M | +5% on €58M = €61M | **€80M → −11%** |

**Biggest Japan normalization losers (% of Japan):** Kering (−22%), LVMH/Richemont/Prada (~−20%). **Biggest absolute hit:** LVMH (~€−1.4B). **Most resilient:** Cucinelli, Burberry (lowest tourist dependency in Japan).

---

| Rank | Group | Quality Drivers (R6 composite) |

| 1 | **Hermès** | #1 organic quality, full-price share, resale retention, VIC insulation; well-balanced Japan exposure |
| 2 | **Brunello Cucinelli** | High organic quality, lowest Chinese exposure, founder-led discipline, lowest Japan normalization risk |

## Q2. China Revenue Geographic Arbitrage Math

| # | Group | (a) Mainland China Revenue (est.) | (b) Chinese-Origin Global Spend (est.) | (c) Chinese % of Global Revenue |

**Key evidence**:
- Bain: Chinese mainland luxury market declined 18–20% in 2024; ~40% of Chinese luxury spending occurs overseas ([Bain China 2024](https://www.bain.com/insights/2024-china-luxury-goods-market/)).
- Burberry: "Mainland Chinese customer group fell −12% in Q4, with tourism accounting for almost a quarter of the customer group sales globally." Japan tourist spend "more than doubled, accounting for half of region's sales in Q4" ([Burberry FY24]).
- LVMH: "Japan saw double-digit revenue growth; the rest of Asia reflected strong growth in spending by Chinese customers in Europe and Japan" ([LVMH PR]).
- Hermès Asia ex-Japan: 44% of revenue at €6.65B. Chinese share elevated given Birkin/Kelly waitlist dynamics.
- Hermès Japan +22.5% constant, partially Chinese tourist-driven.

**Key insight**: Hermès has the highest % of revenue from Chinese-origin customers globally (~33-36%), despite moderate mainland presence, because Chinese VICs buy Hermès everywhere (Paris, Tokyo, HK). Brunello Cucinelli has the lowest Chinese exposure (~14-17%), concentrated in Americas/Europe.

## Q6. Second-Hand Value Retention Index

Data from **Rebag Clair Report 2024** (proprietary algorithm using millions of transactions; value retention = avg resale price ÷ avg retail price):

|------|--------------|--------------------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------|
| 🥇 | **Hermès** | **100%** | Birkin Sellier 250%, Kelly Mini II 150% | Maximum — dictates terms to wholesale |
| 🥈 | **Louis Vuitton (LVMH)** | **88%** | Neverfull 158%, Speedy/Keepall high | Very strong — selective wholesale |
| 🥉 | **Chanel** (benchmark only) | **92%** | Classic Flap ~120% | Very strong |
| 4 | **Saint Laurent (Kering)** | **~75%** | Loulou, Sac de Jour | Moderate-strong |

| 6 | **Cartier (Richemont)** | **~75–80% est.** | Love bracelet, Tank watch | Very strong in jewelry |

**Source**: Rebag Clair Report 2024 ([Rebag](https://www.rebag.com/clair-report/2024/)), PR Newswire release ([Dec 11, 2024](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/rebag-releases-its-fifth-annual-clair-report-a-comprehensive-luxury-appraisal-index-for-resale-302329096.html)).

Burberry's ~50% retention means wholesale partners demand 60%+ markdown guarantees. Brands in the "unicorn" tier (≥85% retention: Hermès, LV, Chanel) have fundamentally different economics from those below 70%.

## Q7. VIC Spend Elasticity to Macroeconomic Conditions

**VIC Elasticity** = (FY24 VIC-attributed revenue Δ%) / (Chinese top-1% wealth Δ%). Lower number = more insulated.

| 8 | **Burberry** | −15 to −20% | **~1.9 to 2.5** | Most elastic. Aspirational-heavy. Sales −1% comparable, China Q4 −17% for locals. Price-point more exposed. |

**Most VIC-protected**: **Hermès** (Birkin/Kelly clientele wealth is globally diversified, not just China-dependent)
**Least VIC-protected**: **Burberry** (higher proportion of aspirational consumers, lower ultra-wealthy penetration)

## Q8. Japan 2025 Normalization Scenario

**Assumptions**: JPY strengthens to 140 (vs ~152 avg 2024, ~160 trough). Chinese inbound tourism to Japan −40% spend (vs +50% in 2024). Domestic Japanese consumption +5%. FX translation headwind on Japan revenue: ~−8% (140 vs ~152 avg).

## Q7. VIC Spend Elasticity to Macroeconomic Conditions

**Methodology:** VIC elasticity = (FY24 VIC revenue Δ) / (Chinese top-1% wealth Δ). Chinese top-1% wealth declined ~5-8% in 2024 (real estate devaluation, equity markets, RMB depreciation). Lower elasticity = more insulated.
